depth_justification: Every follow-up was the same templated re-identification question, mechanically re-tagged [P2.D3] with a bolted-on 'EU AI Act Art. 5(2) data minimization / MDR Art. 12' clause that is mis-applied (AI Act Art. 5 covers prohibited practices, not minimization), and it never drilled into the developer's specific disclosures (Art. 89/Swiss HRA reliance, inability to claw back consortium rows, opaque consortium access). The final report does fold in some InflamaTrack-specific facts (direct-identifier-only stripping, no k-anonymity, all-or-nothing opt-in, missing DPO/DPIA), lifting it above pure generic, but the regulatory anchoring is templated and inaccurate.
actionability_justification: A few mitigations name concrete techniques a developer could start on (k-anonymity/differential privacy plus a statistical re-identification audit, a per-user data-access audit trail, a named consortium member list, a dynamic consent dashboard), which is directional-to-implementable. But most are bare one-liners without recipes, thresholds, or where-to-document guidance, and the repeatedly recycled 'MDR Article 12' tag adds no implementable substance, keeping it solid-directional rather than concrete.
salient_examples: What specific mechanisms are in place to ensure transparency and accountability for data access by the research consortium, and how does this align with the EU AI Act's Article 5(3) on transparency and the MDR's Article 12 on risk management for data handling? [P2.D3]
Implement k-anonymity or differential privacy techniques, and conduct a statistical audit to ensure compliance with GDPR Article 4(1) and MDR Article 12.
Develop a dynamic consent dashboard allowing users to opt in/out of specific data types, aligning with EU AI Act Article 5(2) and MDR Article 12.
Appoint a DPO and conduct a DPIA as required by GDPR Article 30 and MDR Article 12.
